newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai bank predicts new baht attacks in August.
newsitem.headline: Thai bank predicts new baht attacks in August.

text.p: The Siam Commercial Bank Plc said the baht may come under renewed attacks in mid-August amid sustained bearish sentiment over Thailand's ailing economy and troubles faced by financial institutions.

Siam Commercial Bank said in a report received on Monday that currency speculators who attacked the baht in May would probably try to sell the currency short in August after their previous three-month forward positions against the baht expired in that month.

The bank estimated that Thailand used a maximum of five billion dollars of its foreign reserves in May when the Bank of Thailand, helped by regional central banks, was forced to defend the currency from speculative attacks.
Thai foreign reserves fell to a two-year low of $33.3 billion at end-May from $37.3 billion a month earlier.

Speculative hedge funds selling baht short in May lost heavily after the Thai central bank blocked foreign access to local baht supplies, forcing foreign speculators to pay high forward baht/dollar swap rates to fulfill their contracts.

The bank said the spread for the baht exchange rate under a two-tier, onshore and offshore exchange rate system may widen sharply again in August if speculators would be required to raise more offshore baht to meet obligations in forward positions taken three months earlier.
